title: Zoom input dispatch (mouse wheel, pinch accumulation) and zoom/orbit signal wiring have zero test coverage
evidence:
scripts/input_router.gd:36-45:
		and (event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_UP or event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_DOWN):
		zoom_requested.emit(1 if event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_UP else -1)
	elif event is InputEventMagnifyGesture:
		# Trackpad pinch: accumulate the factor, one ladder step per threshold.
		_pinch_accum *= event.factor
		if _pinch_accum >= PINCH_STEP_FACTOR:
			_pinch_accum = 1.0
			zoom_requested.emit(1)
		elif _pinch_accum <= 1.0 / PINCH_STEP_FACTOR:
			_pinch_accum = 1.0

Only direct rig calls exist in tests (grep over tests/ for WHEEL|Magnify|zoom_requested matches nothing; test_camera.gd:55-63):
	_rig.zoom(1)
	check(approx(_rig._target_distance, 15.5), "ladder step in -> district stop")
detail: E1.2/README pin scroll/pinch zoom as a slice-1 control, but only OrbitCamera.zoom() is unit-tested. The router's wheel branch, the stateful pinch-accumulation logic (threshold crossing, reset), and main.gd's zoom_requested.connect(rig.zoom) wiring are never exercised; a regression there passes the suite.
recommended_fix: Extend test_gesture-style parsed-event coverage: send InputEventMouseButton wheel and InputEventMagnifyGesture sequences through InputRouter in the real scene and assert rig zoom-stop changes (and orbit_moved routing).

title: r1 B1 placement-separation fix (full-minimum decay, 25% floor) has no regression test
evidence:
scripts/world_seed.gd:26,143-146:
const MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD := 0.25 # keeps node hitboxes (r 0.95) from overlapping
...		# Separation decays deterministically across attempts (25% floor) so
		# dense layouts still place while early attempts keep full separation.
		var sep := MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD * maxf(1.0 - float(attempt) / 80.0, 0.25)

test_no_sim.gd:57-68 asserts only orientation/layer/determinism (grep 'MIN_NODE|separation' in tests/ matches nothing):
	check(orient_ok, "node bases align to their surface normals")
	check(layer_ok, "nodes sit on physics layer 2 (the press-to-draw grammar)")
	check(same, "node placement is seed-deterministic")
detail: The spec change log records B1 as 'decay the FULL MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD with a 25% floor' to stop overlapping pick hitboxes undermining the disambiguation contract. No test asserts pairwise angular separation of staged sites, so this r1 blocker fix is unpinned against regression.
recommended_fix: In test_no_sim._world_built, assert every staged site pair satisfies Geodesic.arc_angle >= MIN_NODE_SEPARATION_RAD * 0.25 (and hitbox disjointness), pinning the B1 invariant.

test_gesture.gd drives commit/cancel/empty/sky/focus-loss releases but never a release over the source node (no 'pipe_count(a, a)' or source-release assertion anywhere in tests/).

title: merged_params caps (radius 2.2, strands 9) never exercised — only counts 2-3 tested
evidence:
scripts/pipe_arc.gd:42-43:
func merged_params(count: int) -> Array:
	return [minf(1.0 + 0.45 * float(count - 1), 2.2), mini(3 * count, 9)]

test_no_sim.gd:93-100 exercises only count 2 and 3:
	check(controller.pipe_count(a, b) == 2, "parallel pipes register under one bundle")
	check(arc._radius_scale > 1.0, "merged bundle renders fatter")
	...
	controller.connect_programmatic(b, a)
	check(controller.pipe_count(a, b) == 3, "A->B and B->A share the bundle key")
detail: The bundle-growth boundary (cap at 2.2x radius / 9 strands for high parallel counts, per the docstring 'capped so extreme pipe counts stay sane') is never reached in tests; cap regressions would go unnoticed.
recommended_fix: Extend _parallel_merge to commit ~4+ pipes and assert merged_params caps: radius_scale <= 2.2 and strand count <= 9.

title: Damped easing (EASE_RATE convergence in _process) is unasserted — tests bypass it
evidence:
scripts/orbit_camera.gd:61-76:
func _process(delta: float) -> void:
	var k := 1.0 - exp(-EASE_RATE * delta)
	_azimuth = lerp_angle(_azimuth, _target_azimuth, k)
...
func snap() -> void:
	_azimuth = _target_azimuth
...
	_apply_pose(_azimuth, _latitude, _distance)

test_camera.gd applies poses directly, bypassing easing:
	_rig._apply_pose(_rig._target_azimuth, _rig._target_latitude, 14.0)
detail: E1.2 specifies 'damped easing' and 'eases between stops'; every camera test calls _apply_pose/snap() directly. No test asserts the rig converges toward targets over frames, so easing regressions (EASE_RATE, lerp) pass the suite. Tuning-flagged, hence P3.
recommended_fix: Add a test: set targets, await process frames, assert current distance/azimuth approach targets monotonically and converge within tolerance.
